# Verdict and impact ceilings

<!-- GENERATED by `npm run docs:verdicts` from src/utils/verdict.js and the rule registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every finding passes through `settleFinding` (src/utils/verdict.js) before it is reported:

- An axe `incomplete` result (axe could not decide) is `needs-review`, impact at most `moderate`.
- `confirmed` needs a deterministic rule and a recorded `evidence.proof` (a measured or structural fact); without a proof it is `likely`. A rule that measures a rendered state (accessScan `automation: behavioral`, e.g. focus obscured by a sticky bar) gets no fallback proof: its check must record the measurement (elementFromPoint, bounding boxes), else the finding is `likely`.
- `confirmed` needs a measured proof for any owner (site, platform, third-party): `evidence.proof.type` must be one of computed-ratio, attribute-value, name-vs-text, measured-fact, element-from-point, http-status. A validator rule id (`validator-rule`), an engine's generic help text (`dom-structure`) or a rule rationale (`rule-fact`) is not a measurement, so the finding is `needs-review`. A `measured-fact` must hold a measured value (a number, a quoted attribute/id/text, a CSS declaration): an accessScan row whose proof is only the rule rationale and an opening tag that holds no attribute value or number (for example `<title />: the title element is present and non-empty or not`) is downgraded to a `dom-structure` proof and is `needs-review` until its check records a measurement; third-party and platform findings that are confirmed stay outside the gate unless `gate.countThirdParty` / `gate.countPlatform`. A layer's message counts as measured only when it records this instance's value (axe failure summary, a quoted id/attribute/text in an html-validate or w3c message, Lighthouse's per-node explanation).
- A heuristic rule is `needs-review`, impact at most `moderate`; a manual rule is `needs-review`.
- `confirmed` means a WCAG A/AA failure on that element as rendered. An advisory rule (an axe or Lighthouse rule tagged `best-practice` without a WCAG A/AA tag, plus `heading-order`, `page-has-heading-one`, `skip-link`, `tabindex` by id) is `likely` at most: a recommendation, still exported as a task by default (only `needs-review` findings need `--include-needs-review`), never counted by the gate or `--fail-on-violations`. Our own best-practice rules `multiple-navs-missing-labels`, `landmark-unique`, `ListEmpty`, `missing-main-landmark`, `multiple-main-landmarks` (1.3.6 is AAA; 2.4.1 is met by headings or a skip link), `dialog-no-label` (axe `aria-dialog-name` is best-practice, a dialog is a container, not an operable 4.1.2 component) and `tabs-missing-aria-controls` (APG advice) (any layer) are `needs-review`: not counted by the gate and not exported as fix tasks unless `--include-needs-review`. Rules left `confirmed` when measured: every axe rule that carries a wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa tag (for example `bypass`, `color-contrast`, `document-title`, `image-alt`, `label`, `link-name`, `button-name`), `image-alt-missing-sr`, `html-missing-lang`, `page-missing-title`.
- Rules that are real but not provably an A/AA failure are `likely` at most (`empty-heading`, `modal-focus-escapes`, `modal-focus-not-trapped`, `skip-link-target-missing`): `empty-heading` is axe best-practice; `modal-focus-escapes` and `modal-focus-not-trapped` map to 2.4.3 (leaving a modal is the opposite of a 2.1.2 keyboard trap; APG pattern) and an escape does not count when focus lands on a control inside the dialog's own position:fixed overlay wrapper (a close button drawn beside the dialog); `skip-link-target-missing` is a broken skip link, but a main landmark or headings already bypass the blocks (2.4.1) and the keyboard check does not record that, so it cannot confirm.
- A behavioural-layer row (keyboard, focusTrap, ariaLive, dynamicContent, screenReader) is confirmed only when its check wrote `evidence.proof`: its description is wording, never a measurement, so a row with no recorded proof gets a `dom-structure` proof and is `needs-review`. Keyboard rows whose check measured but records no proof field (`focus-not-visible` with its pixel comparison, `focus-invisible-stop` landed, `skip-link-missing`) get the proof from the index adapter (`keyboardEvidence`), only when the check did not leave them `needs-review`. `focus-indicator-removed` is a stylesheet guess with no proof, so it is `needs-review`.
- `focus-obscured` (accessScan `FocusNotObscured*`, `StickyHeaderObscuresFocus`): a bar that is translucent at the sampled points (background alpha below 1, `backdrop-filter`, opacity below 1, with no opaque element on top) leaves the control readable through it, and 2.4.11 only fails when it is entirely hidden, so the row is `needs-review`.
- `disclosure-missing-aria-expanded` and `menu-trigger-missing-aria-expanded` are confirmed only when the panel was found through `aria-controls` or as an adjacent sibling, its visibility flipped (shown, `hidden` or `aria-hidden`), it is not a dialog (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, role dialog, `aria-modal`, `<dialog>`: APG needs no aria-expanded) and the control has no `aria-pressed`. A height-only change, a page-wide drawer fallback target, a dialog trigger or a toggle button is `needs-review`.

- `confirmed` on a site-owned finding also needs a traced source: a source `file:line` with confidence of at least medium (the anchor of an absence finding counts). One without it is `likely` with `untraced: true`, `source.traceReason` and `verdictBeforeAgreement: confirmed` (baseline comparison reads that), shown in the report and exported as a task marked "Untraced: locate manually" with its candidates; the harness G1 gate still counts a new untraced finding as a regression. This applies to local scans with a source adapter (`runMetadata.sourceTracing.requireSource`); remote scans, scans with no source project, and vendor or platform findings are unchanged.
- `skip-link-missing` (keyboard layer) is confirmed only when no bypass mechanism exists: 3+ repeated header/nav stops before the content, no skip link, no main landmark and no headings. Landmark navigation (ARIA11) and headings (H69) are sufficient techniques for 2.4.1, so a page with a main landmark or headings gets `likely`; fewer repeated stops stay `needs-review`.
- A behavioural rule may downgrade a single row below its kind: `focus-lost-after-escape` is `likely` when focus is on the body but the next Tab continues near the trigger (confirmed only when one Tab restarts at the top of the page or lands far from the trigger), `focus-indicator-removed` is `needs-review` unless a confirmed `focus-not-visible` pixel proof backs an element its selector matches, and `reflow-horizontal-scroll` is `needs-review` for wide fixed-position content (the document itself does not scroll). The rule-level kind below is the best case; `docs/measured-checks.md` states each condition.
- Dead links (`dead-link-*`, `broken-link`) are a QA defect, not a WCAG failure: they carry `category: reliability`, so the accessibility threshold gate (`a11y.*`, which counts `category: accessibility` only) and the accessibility precision leave them out. Decision: `--fail-on-violations` still fails on a confirmed dead link (it counts every confirmed finding, as before); the threshold gate does not.
- Per-rule impact ceilings: `duplicate-id-aria` <= serious, `dialog-missing-aria-modal` <= moderate, `modal-focus-escapes` <= serious, `modal-focus-not-trapped` <= serious, `TabAriaControls` <= minor, `TabpanelLabelledBy` <= minor, `NoAutofocus` <= minor, `TableNesting` <= minor, `RegionMainContentSingle` <= minor, `NoRoleApplication` <= minor, `NoExtraInformationInTitle` <= minor, `FocusNotObscuredFooter` <= serious, `FocusNotObscuredHeader` <= serious, `StickyHeaderObscuresFocus` <= serious.

What a deterministic row of each family becomes (`npm run docs:verdicts` evaluates `scripts/lib/proof-families.js`; the rows marked needs-review are the ones downgraded from confirmed):

| Family | Proof type | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| axe, per-node failure summary | measured-fact | confirmed |
| axe, measured contrast | computed-ratio | confirmed |
| axe, generic help only | dom-structure | needs-review |
| html-validate / w3c, message quotes the value | measured-fact | confirmed |
| html-validate / w3c, rule wording only | validator-rule | needs-review |
| lighthouse, per-node explanation | measured-fact | confirmed |
| lighthouse, rule id only | validator-rule | needs-review |
| visible text vs accessible name captured | name-vs-text | confirmed |
| layer-recorded proof | http-status | confirmed |
| accessScan, measured-fact holding a measured value | measured-fact | confirmed |
| accessScan, measured-fact that is only the rule rationale and the opening tag | dom-structure | needs-review |
| behavioural rule, instance description only (check recorded no proof) | dom-structure | needs-review |
| behavioural rule, proof recorded by the check | attribute-value | confirmed |
| behavioural rule, no instance text | none | likely |
